headline: Weekend US-Iran strikes shatter the interim peace deal: oil surges ~4% overnight, equity futures slide, and Treasuries sell off as rate-hike bets intensify ahead of Tuesday's CPI.
stance: The weekend's multi-wave exchange of strikes — the US hitting 300+ Iranian targets, Iran retaliating against Gulf bases and declaring the Strait of Hormuz closed — has snapped the fragile truce and repriced risk across every asset class. The dominant question for this week is whether Tuesday's June CPI (consensus: headline ~3.9%, core ~0.3% m/m) validates the hawkish drift already embedded in futures, or delivers a modest relief print that lets markets stabilise ahead of the big-bank earnings wave. Until the geopolitical fog clears, headline risk is high and energy/rate volatility will set the tone.

news.head: US-Iran: ceasefire in tatters
news.body: Over the weekend, the US launched a fourth-plus wave of strikes on Iranian targets — hitting Bandar Abbas, petrochemical sites, air-defence and drone facilities — while Iran retaliated with strikes on US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, Oman and Qatar, and again declared the Strait of Hormuz closed; US CENTCOM disputed the closure claim, saying shipping continues on the southern route.

news.head: Oil surges ~4% overnight
news.body: OVERNIGHT LEVEL: Brent crude futures near $79 per barrel and WTI near $74 per barrel, each up roughly 4% from Friday's prior cash close (Brent $76, WTI $71.51), on fears of a genuine Hormuz supply disruption.

news.head: Gold slides despite the war escalation
news.body: OVERNIGHT LEVEL: Gold fell as much as 1.4% to near $4,060/oz — counterintuitively lower from Friday's prior cash close of $4,129 — because higher oil re-fires inflation fears, which supports a hawkish Fed, lifts real yields, and that is gold's main headwind in 2026.

news.head: Equity futures in the red
news.body: OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET: S&P 500 futures are down roughly 0.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures down roughly 1.2%, and Dow futures down roughly 0.4% from Friday's prior cash closes (SPX 7,575, NDX 26,282, DJI 52,637).

news.head: Treasuries sell off; 2Y hits post-Feb high
news.body: OVERNIGHT LEVEL: The 2-year Treasury yield climbed ~3 bps to roughly 4.23% — the highest since February 2025 — while the 10-year yield also moved higher across the curve, versus Friday's prior cash closes of 2Y 4.21% and 10Y 4.56%.

news.head: Rate-hike bets ratchet up
news.body: Swaps are now pricing roughly 40 basis points of Fed hikes by December 2026 — up from about 15 bps in early June — and markets assign roughly 62% odds of a hike at the September meeting, reinforced by hawkish June FOMC minutes released last week.

news.head: Big-bank earnings start Tuesday
news.body: JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Citigroup and Goldman Sachs all report Tuesday, with Morgan Stanley and BlackRock on Wednesday — the Q2 season is expected to show a second straight quarter of earnings growth above 20%.

news.head: CPI & Fed Chair Warsh on Tuesday
news.body: June CPI (consensus headline ~3.9%, core ~0.3% m/m) lands Tuesday morning alongside Fed Chair Warsh's first semi-annual congressional testimony — the last major inflation print before the Fed meets later this month.

implications: Oil above $74 (WTI) re-opens the inflation-via-energy channel; if Tuesday's CPI core comes in at 0.3% m/m or hotter, the market will move the September hike probability materially higher and compress equity multiples — particularly in rate-sensitive growth stocks.

The equity sell-off is tech-led (Nasdaq futures -1.2% vs S&P -0.5%), consistent with duration-sensitive names bearing the brunt of rising rate expectations; energy stocks and tanker names should outperform at the open.

Strait of Hormuz ambiguity is the key unknown: US CENTCOM insists shipping is flowing; Iran insists it is closed. Any confirmation of a real blockade would be a step-change, not a continuation — current oil prices do not yet price a full closure.

Gold's counter-intuitive drop is a regime signal: in this cycle, geopolitical risk that raises oil and therefore inflation expectations is net-negative for gold, because the Fed hawkish response lifts real yields — gold's ceiling in 2026.

The dollar (DXY ~101, pre-market vs prior cash close 100.96) is catching a mild safe-haven bid; USD/JPY is pinned above 161 overnight (prior cash close 161.67), and EUR/USD is near 1.1404 (prior cash close 1.1419) — yen is outperforming G10 peers on geopolitical flight.

Positioning: In rates, speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3M SOFR (2nd percentile of 3 years — a contrarian floor); in equities, the same is true for Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile — a contrarian floor). In FX, British Pound speculative positioning is at a 3-year short extreme (2nd percentile, divergence with hedgers — a contrarian floor for GBP). In commodities, copper speculators are extended long at the 94th percentile — a contrarian warning, especially with copper already at an extreme 97th-percentile price level.

watch.head: Tuesday 8:30am ET — June CPI
watch.body: The single most important print of the week: consensus is headline ~3.9% and core ~0.3% m/m; a beat on core would likely cement a September rate hike and extend Monday's equity and bond selling.

watch.head: Tuesday — Warsh congressional testimony
watch.body: Fed Chair Warsh's first semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins appearance before Congress; watch for any signal on whether renewed oil-driven inflation shifts the Fed's 'wait and watch' posture toward an explicit hike bias.

watch.head: Tuesday — JPM, GS, WFC, BAC, C earnings
watch.body: Five major banks report in the same morning; strong capital-markets revenue is expected — any guidance cautioning on credit quality or net-interest-margin pressure in a higher-for-longer rate environment will be the key surprise risk.

watch.head: Hormuz shipping status — intraday
watch.body: Watch CENTCOM statements and Lloyd's / maritime agency vessel-tracking reports for whether commercial tanker transits through the strait actually halt; that binary outcome will drive oil and the broader risk-off/risk-on tone all week.

watch.head: Wednesday — June PPI
watch.body: Producer prices (consensus -0.2% m/m, +6.2% YoY) land the day after CPI; together the two prints will set final rate-path expectations before the Fed's next meeting.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: PRIOR CASH CLOSE (Fri Jul 10): 10Y Treasury yield 4.56%, 2Y yield 4.21%; yield curve (2s10s) +35 bps — positively sloped but slim, consistent with a late-cycle slow-growth regime.

OVERNIGHT LEVEL: 2Y yield has risen ~3 bps to roughly 4.23% — highest since February 2025 — as oil's surge re-fires inflation fears and the market prices a higher probability of a Fed hike by September (now ~62%).
Real rates remain elevated at 2.32% (prior cash close); this is the structural headwind for growth equities and gold, and an oil shock that keeps inflation sticky only extends this constraint.

The 10-year breakeven inflation expectation (prior cash close: 2.24%) will likely tick higher Monday as energy reprices — watch this vs the 4.56% nominal yield for how the bond market splits the oil shock between 'inflation' and 'growth fear'.

MOVE index (bond-market volatility gauge) at 69.5 (prior cash close) is calm relative to recent peaks — but a hot CPI or an escalated Hormuz closure would push this sharply higher, which would ripple into credit spreads.

Term premium (how much extra yield investors demand to hold long bonds) stands at 73.2 bps — elevated and rising; this is partly a fiscal concern (Treasury General Account $774bn, reserves $3,099bn) and partly a geopolitical risk premium.

Financial conditions remain loose overall: the Chicago Fed's financial conditions index is -0.51 z-scores (easy) and the St. Louis Fed stress index is -0.72 (low stress) — but that was before this weekend's escalation.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left on 3M SOFR interest-rate futures — a 3-year low (2nd percentile) and the most extreme short position in the complex, sitting opposite to hedgers who are heavily long. This is a contrarian signal that the rate market may be over-pricing Fed hikes; a softer CPI print Tuesday could trigger a sharp rally in short-dated bonds.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: PRIOR CASH CLOSE (Fri Jul 10): S&P 500 at 7,575, Nasdaq 100 at 26,282, Dow at 52,637 — all at or near record highs, with the S&P up ~11% year-to-date.
OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET: S&P 500 futures -0.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures -1.2%, Dow futures -0.4% — tech is leading the decline as rising rate-hike expectations hit the highest-duration growth names hardest.

PRIOR CASH CLOSE breadth check: 65.8% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 50-day average and 68.1% above their 200-day average — solid internal strength, meaning the index is not being carried by just a handful of mega-caps.

VIX (fear gauge — how much the options market is paying for S&P insurance) at 15.03 (prior cash close) is low and complacent; a geopolitical shock of this magnitude at 15 VIX means options are cheap to buy heading into a risk event, and a spike toward 20+ is feasible.

SKEW at 144.3 (prior cash close) is elevated — institutional investors are paying up for tail-risk protection (out-of-the-money puts), signalling that even with a low VIX the smart money is not fully complacent about a sharp drawdown.
Equity risk premium (ERP) is -2.05% — stocks are paying less than bonds after adjusting for risk, a structural caution flag; this makes equities more vulnerable to any upside yield surprise from CPI.

CAPE (the long-run valuation ratio that smooths earnings over 10 years) is 42.18 — historically stretched — but as BMO noted, recent S&P gains are earnings-driven rather than multiple-expansion, which is a healthier composition.

Q2 earnings season opens in earnest Tuesday; a second straight quarter of 20%+ earnings growth is expected — the bull case depends on results validating that growth story while the bears point to oil-driven margin pressure.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left on Russell 2000 (small-cap) futures — a 3-year low at the 2nd percentile — sitting opposite to hedgers; this is a contrarian floor for small-caps. If CPI comes in tame and rate-hike fears fade, small-caps carry the most coiled upside from a positioning squeeze.

single_name.note: CarMax (used-auto retailer) — highest-conviction long setup: large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) confirmed, a burst of unusual options buying confirmed, 2 company insider buying rules fired, and the stock is trading above its 200-day average. Shorts are not heavy (4.4 days to cover), limiting squeeze risk but also reducing friction on a move higher. Signal is fresh as of July 10.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield vs investment-grade spread at 270 bps (prior cash close Jul 9) — credit markets are not yet flashing distress; for context, IG option-adjusted spread is 76 bps (prior cash close), both calm.
Commercial paper spread (CPFF) at 18 bps (prior cash close) — short-term funding markets are not stressed; interbank plumbing (FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS both -9 bps) is clean.

Bank credit growth is running at 5.93% year-over-year (as of Jul 1) and the leveraged-loan market is clearing at 6.98% (as of Jul 9) — credit supply is flowing, but loan rates this high create a slow-burn drag on capital-intensive businesses.

M2 money supply growing 5.58% YoY (as of May) with Fed balance sheet +1.1% YoY — liquidity is not being actively withdrawn, but the reverse-repo facility is nearly drained ($0.5bn, prior cash close), meaning that structural liquidity support is exhausted.

Bank reserves at $3,099bn (as of Jul 8) and TGA at $774bn — the Treasury has firepower; watch for any large TGA drawdown (spending) as a source of reserve injection that could ease money-market conditions.

ISM Manufacturing at 53.3 and Services PMI at 54.5 — both above the 50-line that separates contraction from expansion — means the real economy is still growing into this geopolitical shock, limiting the case for an imminent recession-driven credit blowup.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers (product tanker operator) — directly exposed to the Hormuz disruption thesis: large off-exchange block buying and unusual options buying both live, 2 insider buying rules fired, trading above 200-day average. Shorts are moderate (4 days to cover). Signal is aging (88% weight remaining). An oil/shipping geopolitical shock is exactly the macro environment this name is set up for.
